design.text: Randomized, double-masked, multicenter, active-controlled (brimonidine), parallel-group study

indication.text: VIZZ is indicated for the treatment of presbyopia in adults.

citations.quote: VIZZ is indicated for the treatment of presbyopia in adults.

target_moa.text: Cholinergic muscarinic (M3) receptor agonist; a pupil-selective miotic that contracts the iris sphincter muscle producing a pinhole effect that extends depth of focus

citations.quote: Aceclidine is a cholinergic muscarinic agonist that stimulates muscarinic receptors located on smooth muscles.
VIZZ causes contraction of the iris sphincter muscle, resulting in a pinhole effect that extends depth of focus to improve vision.
Aceclidine is predicated on its action on the muscarinic 3 (M3) receptors found on the iris sphincter

Aceclidine is a muscarinic acetylcholine receptor agonist and exerts its action as a pupil-selective miotic by acting on and contracting the pupil sphincter muscle, creating a “pinhole effect” that enhances depth of focus and improves near vision in presbyopia.

modality.text: Small molecule; VIZZ is aceclidine hydrochloride 1.75% (equivalent to 1.44% aceclidine) ophthalmic solution (the LNZ100 monotherapy arm), not the LNZ101 aceclidine+brimonidine combination

citations.quote: VIZZ (aceclidine ophthalmic solution) 1.44% is a cholinergic muscarinic receptor agonist supplied as a sterile, clear to opalescent, colorless to slightly yellow, and viscous ophthalmic solution containing 1.75% of aceclidine hydrochloride (equivalent to 1.44% aceclidine).

The review team did not identify any issues with assessing superiority of LNZ100 over brimonidine (CLARITY-1) or vehicle (CLARITY-2) for the primary efficacy endpoint (improvement of 3 lines [15 letters] or greater at 40 cm and no loss \ge 5 letters at 4 m in monocular BCVA at Visit 2

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions: instillation site irritation (20%), dim vision (16%), headache (13%); conjunctival hyperemia (8%) and ocular hyperemia (7%) in >5%

citations.quote: The most common reported adverse reactions of participants were instillation site irritation (20%), dim vision (16%), and headache (13%). Adverse reactions reported in > 5% of participants were conjunctival hyperemia (8%) and ocular hyperemia (7%). The majority of adverse reactions were mild, transient, and self-resolving.
